compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The Bedrock spend cap prices `claude-sonnet-4-5` at the deliberately-high fail-closed fallback
rather than its real rate, because the seed-rate table pins exact minor versions for the Claude
Sonnet and Haiku families. The cap therefore over-meters that model and trips earlier than the
configured threshold intends.

Observed in the handler's own log output:

```
no rate for model=...claude-sonnet-4-5 metric=...; using fail-closed fallback
```

## Root cause

`_seed_for()` in `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py:277` matches by **substring**:

```python
for needle, prices in SEED_RATES.items():
    if needle not in model_id:
        continue
```

The needles come from `var.bedrock_cap_seed_rates` in `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:63`:

```hcl
default = {
  "claude-haiku-4-5"  = { input = 0.0011, output = 0.0055 }
  "claude-sonnet-4-6" = { input = 0.0033, output = 0.0165 }
  "claude-opus"       = { input = 0.0055, output = 0.0275 }
}
```

`"claude-sonnet-4-6" not in "...claude-sonnet-4-5"` is true, so the loop falls through, `_seed_for`
returns `None`, and line 357 returns `MeteredRate(rate=UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K * mult, source="fallback")`.
The handler's own docstring at line 44 states `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K` is "set deliberately HIGH so
unpriced models fail closed" — correct as a safety default, wrong as the steady-state price for a
model the project actually runs.

### The table is internally inconsistent, and that is the real defect

Two of the 3 entries are version-pinned (`claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`) while the third
is a bare family (`claude-opus`), which matches every Opus version by substring. So Opus is already
version-resilient and the other 2 families are not — the same ladder bump that breaks Sonnet leaves
Opus working. Adding `claude-sonnet-4-5` as a fourth pinned entry would fix today's symptom and
leave the mechanism just as brittle for `-4-7`.

This mirrors a distinction the codebase already draws deliberately elsewhere:
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:235` comments that its table keys on "the family, not the full
pinned id, so a ladder version bump (`claude-sonnet-4-6` → `-4-7`) keeps" working. The spend cap did
not adopt that convention.

## Impact

The cap is load-bearing for agent operations — the delivery loop reads this meter and pauses all
work when its alert fires. Over-metering means work can be paused on a spend figure that is inflated
rather than real, and the inflation is silent apart from a `log.warning` nobody reads. The failure
direction is safe, which is exactly why it can persist unnoticed.

## Investigation notes for whoever takes this

`_seed_for` is only the fallback's last step; the docstring at line 317 describes a 4-level ladder
(empirical, seed, empirical_scaled, fallback). Confirm which level actually served the observed
request before changing the table — an empirical rate should have taken precedence if the account
had billing history for that model, so its absence may itself be informative.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The root cause is confirmed by reproducing the fallback selection for a `claude-sonnet-4-5` model id, with the observed `RateSource` recorded, rather than inferred from reading the table.
- [ ] Establish and record why the empirical rate did not serve this model, since that level precedes the seed table.
- [ ] Seed-rate lookup is resilient to a model ladder version bump, so a new minor version does not silently fall back to the high fail-closed rate. Fixing only `claude-sonnet-4-5` by adding a fourth pinned key does not satisfy this.
- [ ] The Opus/Sonnet/Haiku entries follow one consistent keying convention; the current mix of family-level and version-pinned keys is resolved either way with the choice justified.
- [ ] A test covers a model id whose version is newer than any table entry and asserts it is priced from its family rather than the fallback.
- [ ] A genuinely unknown model family still receives the fail-closed fallback — the safety property must survive the fix.
- [ ] Selecting the fallback for a model the project actually runs is surfaced more loudly than a `log.warning`, so silent over-metering cannot persist.
compiled_state.title: Bedrock spend cap over-meters claude-sonnet-4-5: seed rates are version-pinned, so a ladder bump falls back to the high unknown rate
